remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the small-business onboarding limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case or paid pilot commitments.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap before launch.
The affected segment is tied to two paid pilot commitments, which supports materiality under the policy text.
Legal review remains open, so the policy predicate for release-condition compliance is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal support operational readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partly correct: the evidence supports aggregate operational readiness, and the main dispute is the unresolved treatment of the small-business onboarding gap. But that narrower framing is not enough for compliant_with_caveats. A caveated-compliance finding would require the caveat to be non-dispositive or already bounded by evidence showing the required condition was satisfied. Here the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate: policy states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record shows the segment misses target, is named in two paid pilot commitments, and remains under open legal review, while showing no disclosure, no resolution, and no approved risk acceptance. That keeps the certification claim noncompliant on the present record, even if the broader system appears launch-ready in aggregate.
